subject: human bladder
title: What If You Always Held In Your Pee?

scenes.text: What if you always held in your pee? Your brain would slowly stop listening to your bladder.
An adult bladder holds about 400 to 600 millilitres, one to two soda cans.
You first feel the urge at around 200 millilitres, when it's only about half full.
Hold it again and again, and that first signal can shift to around 400. The brain stops noticing.
Urine that sits for hours gives bacteria time to grow, raising the risk of urinary infections.
Over years, a bladder that's always stretched can weaken and struggle to empty. Some people end up needing a catheter.

description:
What if you always held in your pee? Urologists say the brain can learn to ignore a full bladder, moving the first urge from about 200 to about 400 millilitres.
An adult bladder holds roughly 400 to 600 millilitres. Habitual holding is linked to urinary infections, and over time a chronically stretched bladder can become underactive and hard to empty. Doctors suggest emptying it every 3 to 4 hours while awake.
